newsitem.title: GREECE: National Bank's Q1 pretax profit up 80pct.
newsitem.headline: National Bank's Q1 pretax profit up 80pct.

text.p: National Bank, Greece's largest commercial bank, saw first quarter pretax earnings jump 80 percent to 19.7 billion drachmas from 10.7 billion in the same period a year earlier, a high level bank official told Reuters.
"The bank's pretax earnings in the first three months of 1997 have risen around 80 percent to 19.7 billion drachmas against 10.9 billion in the respective period of 1996," the source said.
The strong earnings growth is after loan loss provisions as per regulations, the source added.

In fiscal 1996, the bank minimised its bottom line taking large loan loss provisions of 61.4 billion drachmas in an effort to cleanse its balance sheet. It did not pay a dividend and posted zero profit.
"The bank's bottom line has been boosted by a rise in income from all traditional banking activities," said the source.

"This includes interest and commission income, but mostly gains from portfolio transactions, capitalising on the favourable macroeconomic environment of falling interest rates coupled with rising equity prices in the Athens bourse," the source added.
